issues.title: Virological and epidemiological investigations of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak, Vietnam, 2023
issues.title_en: Virological and epidemiological investigations of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak, Vietnam, 2023
issues.summary: Author summary In 2023, Vietnam experienced a large and severe outbreak of hand food and mouth disease in children. Our investigations showed that enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) subgenogroup B5, first emerging around November 2022, and then introduced into Vietnam through a single event, was the main cause. Blood samples from patients who recovered from subgenogroups B5 infection in 2014 and 2023 could neutralize both contemporary viruses without evidence of immune evasion. Before the start of the outbreak, only 6.7% of 0– < 3 year-old children in Ho Chi Minh City, an epicenter of the outbreak, had neutralizing antibodies that can block EV-A71 infection. Seroprevalence increased as the outbreak progressed, while the number of the infected patients decreased. Monitoring population immunity against EV-A71 could help assess the risk of pathogen emergence. EV-A71 infection represents an ongoing public health threat, currently affecting countries in the Asia-Pacific region, but with a high potential to become a global problem, and therefore should be closely monitored.
